doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: The Afro-Classic Ensemble and its drummer Freddie Waits
summary: Brown opens the LP; Laws recalls his first group, the Afro-Classic Ensemble, with Ron Carter and Freddie Waits.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I’m going to go ahead and bust it open. I’m in your house.
I never took the cellophane off, but I always got the LP out. I always tried to keep the cover. So I’m going to go ahead and bust it out.
You hadn’t even opened it up.
That shows you how I felt about this. I’m trying to preserve it. It’s been 41 years.
It doesn’t seem like it. My first group was called the Afro-Classic Ensemble. Ron Carter was in it. I think Freddie Waits. Is Freddie Waits on that?
His son is now a big, big drummer, Rasheed [Nasheed] Waits. Who chose the personnel? Did you have that? Or was that something that was also negotiated?
